question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are primarily aimed at achieving:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Social and economic justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, aimed at achieving social and economic justice in India.
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The objective of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• These principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state in India.
 
• They cover various aspects such as economic and social rights, Gandhian principles, and policies aimed at establishing international peace and security.
 
• The principles include provisions for securing a living wage, humane conditions of work, social security, and the right to education.
 
• They also advocate for the promotion of the interests of weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
 
 
• **Economic Inequality**
 
 
• Economic inequality refers to the extent of the wealth gap between rich and poor in a society.
 
• This concept is not a focus of the Directive Principles, which aim instead at reducing inequalities through social and economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Religious Harmony**
 
 
• Religious harmony refers to peaceful coexistence and mutual respect among various religions in a society.
 
• While important, this is not the primary aim of the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• **Political Stability**
 
 
• Political stability refers to the consistency and predictability of political institutions and governance.
 
• Although essential for development, this is not the primary aim of the Directive Principles.
